column6: Justification (verified against RFC text)

column3: Ephemeral agent or sub-agent identity
column6: No OAuth RFC defines ephemeral delegates or sub-agents — participants existing only for the duration of a single task or invocation.

column3: Distinguish upstream from downstream delegation participants
column6: No OAuth RFC defines delegation participant lineage semantics. The nested act structure of RFC 8693 §4.1 does not normatively define upstream vs. downstream participant relationships or provide traversal rules.

column3: Preserve accountability across multiple delegation hops
column6: No RFC defines accountability semantics across multiple delegation hops. RFC 8693 act chain informally supports two-hop actor representation; no normative chain integrity requirements exist for longer chains.

column3: Tool-invocation-level authorization constraints
column6: No RFC defines authorization semantics for specific tool invocations, API schemas, or agent tool calls. RFC 9396 authorization_details types are extensible but no normative type for tool-level agent constraints exists.
column7: Gap: requires new normative type definition under RFC 9396 extension or new spec.

column3: Workflow or transaction-scoped delegation constraints
column6: No OAuth RFC defines workflow-bound or transaction-scoped delegation. No normative mechanism binds delegated authority to a specific parent transaction or orchestration context.

column3: Guarantee of authority monotonicity (downstream authority cannot exceed upstream)
column6: No RFC normatively guarantees that downstream delegated authority cannot exceed upstream authority. RFC 8693 §2.1 notes the intent as a design consideration without mandating enforcement.
column7: Gap: requires new normative definition with enforcement mechanism.

column3: Designate a named enforcement actor for each delegation constraint type
column6: No RFC defines a mechanism for associating a specific delegation constraint with a named enforcement actor (AS, RS, Agent Platform, Tool Provider). RFC 9396 implies AS and RS but does not define per-constraint actor designation as a protocol construct.

column3: Define enforcement responsibilities across heterogeneous agent platforms
column6: No RFC defines enforcement responsibilities across agent platform boundaries. The agent platform role does not exist in the OAuth protocol model.

column3: Delegator role (principal granting authority to a delegate)
column6: No RFC introduces 'delegator' as a named protocol role. RFC 8693 implicitly treats the subject_token presenter as the delegating party but defines no distinct delegator role with explicit semantics.

column3: Delegate agent role (software agent receiving and exercising delegated authority)
column6: No RFC defines a 'delegate agent' role for software agents acting autonomously. RFC 8693 defines 'actor' for the token exchanger; this partially overlaps but is not equivalent to an autonomous executing agent.

column3: Downstream delegation participant role
column6: No RFC defines downstream delegation participants as a named protocol role. RFC 8693 §4.1 describes nested act informally; no taxonomy of downstream participant roles is defined.

column3: Delegation ancestry semantics (upstream/downstream participant relationships)
column6: No RFC defines delegation ancestry semantics: traversal rules, chain validation, or the normative relationship between ancestor and descendant delegates.

column3: Downstream delegation lifetime bounded by upstream (monotonic inheritance)
column6: No RFC defines monotonic lifetime inheritance. RFC 8693 does not define any normative relationship between source and derived token expiration; no normative rule requires derived_token.exp ≤ source_token.exp.

column3: Normative relationship between upstream and downstream lifetime constraints
column6: No RFC defines the normative relationship between upstream and downstream delegation lifetime constraints across a multi-hop chain.

column3: Renewal and reauthorization semantics for persistent delegation chains
column6: RFC 6749 defines the refresh_token grant, but no RFC defines renewal or reauthorization semantics specific to delegated authority that persists across multiple agentic execution contexts.

column3: Cascading revocation to downstream delegation artifacts
column6: No RFC defines cascading revocation. RFC 7009 §2.1 mentions associated tokens only in the context of refresh/access token pairs under the same grant — not delegation chains. Revoking a source token via RFC 7009 has no normative effect on downstream tokens derived from it via RFC 8693.

column3: Subtree revocation (invalidating all tokens in a delegation subtree)
column6: No RFC defines subtree revocation semantics.

column3: Partial delegation revocation (revoking specific permissions without full token invalidation)
column6: No RFC defines partial delegation revocation. RFC 7009 operates at the token level, not the permission level.

column3: Revocation behavior during in-progress delegated execution
column6: No RFC defines the protocol behavior when a token is revoked while an agentic task using that token is actively executing.

column3: Delegation ancestry validation across multi-hop chains
column6: No RFC defines a normative procedure for validating delegation ancestry. The nested act structure of RFC 8693 §4.1 is described but no validation rules for traversing or verifying the chain are specified.
column8: Derived ← R4 delegation ancestry semantics; R0 actor-chain representation

column3: Delegation-depth validation
column6: No RFC defines delegation depth limits or a normative validation procedure for enforcing them.

column3: Delegation provenance validation — authenticity and completeness of execution records, including tool invocations, state transitions and human approvals, consistent with delegated authority
column6: No RFC defines provenance validation across multiple delegation hops.
column8: Derived ← R12 execution and tool-invocation provenance

column3: Security consequences of artifact compromise (blast radius, failures, remediation, chains across trust domains)
column6: No RFC defines blast radius or remediation behavior specific to compromised delegation chain artifacts. RFC 7009 defines revocation but not in the context of chain-wide compromise remediation.

column3: Runtime or workload-context binding
column6: No OAuth RFC defines binding of delegated authority to a specific runtime workload, execution environment, or agent instance. SPIFFE SVIDs (informative prior art) provide workload identity but are outside the OAuth corpus.

column3: Rotation and failure behavior for binding credentials — replacing a compromised or expired binding credential (DPoP key pair, mTLS certificate) without invalidating the delegation chain
column6: No published OAuth RFC defines rotation or failure behavior for binding credentials in the context of delegation chains (draft R9(g)).

column3: Formal attenuation algebra (normative rules for deriving downstream from upstream authority)
column6: No RFC defines a formal attenuation algebra or normative derivation rules for delegation authority chains. This is the core attenuation gap.

column3: Monotonic attenuation guarantee (downstream ≤ upstream)
column6: No RFC provides a normative monotonic attenuation guarantee. RFC 8693 §2.1 notes the intent as a design consideration; no enforcement mechanism exists.

column3: Verifiable proof that downstream authority is bounded by upstream authority
column6: No RFC defines a mechanism enabling a relying party to verify that a downstream delegation artifact's authority is a subset of its upstream artifact.

column3: Explicit permission to re-delegate
column6: No RFC defines an explicit permission mechanism enabling a delegate to sub-delegate authority. There is no normative claim, policy mechanism, or protocol field for re-delegation permission.

column3: Explicit prohibition of re-delegation
column6: No RFC defines a normative mechanism for prohibiting re-delegation. A holder of a token obtained via RFC 8693 exchange is not prevented from performing a further exchange.

column3: Delegation depth limits
column6: No RFC defines a maximum delegation depth or a normative max_depth claim or equivalent.

column3: Downstream authority inheritance rules for re-delegated tokens
column6: No RFC defines normative rules governing how a re-delegated token's authority relates to its upstream token's authority.

column3: Execution provenance — state transitions, platform configurations and environments of the agent (linking delegated authority to security-relevant execution events)
column6: No RFC defines execution provenance for agentic systems.

column3: Invocation provenance — logging of explicit requests initiated by intermediary orchestration components
column6: No published OAuth RFC defines logging or recording of explicit requests initiated by intermediary orchestration components (draft R12(d)).

column3: Tool invocation provenance — parameters, schemas and API endpoints called under delegated authority
column6: No RFC defines provenance semantics for tool invocations performed under delegated authority.

column3: Human approval provenance (verifiable attestations of oversight decisions)
column6: No RFC defines provenance semantics for human oversight decisions during delegated execution.

column3: Provenance disclosure semantics (verifiability, mutability, selective disclosure, privacy)
column6: No RFC defines a provenance disclosure framework for delegation chains. RFC 9901 SD-JWT provides selective disclosure for individual JWT claims but not a chain-provenance disclosure model.

column3: Human approval checkpoints during delegated execution
column6: No RFC defines protocol mechanisms for human approval checkpoints within a running delegated execution flow.

column3: Semantics of approval denial, interruption, or override during execution
column6: No RFC defines protocol-level effects of a human denying, interrupting, or overriding a delegated execution in progress.

column3: Human oversight policies (who is authorized to approve, trigger conditions)
column6: No RFC defines authorization semantics for human oversight providers or the conditions under which human involvement is required.

column3: Classification of delegated actions as autonomous vs. supervised
column6: No RFC defines a mechanism to classify delegated actions as requiring human supervision or permitting autonomous execution.

column3: Binding of a human approval to the exact delegated action and its parameters (what is approved is what is executed)
column6: No RFC defines binding of a human approval to the exact action and parameters executed.

column3: Approval validity window and invalidation when the action, parameters or context change between approval and execution (TOCTOU)
column6: No RFC defines an approval validity window or invalidation of an approval when the action, parameters or context change.

column3: Approver unavailability — substitution, delegation of approval authority, multi-party approval, and behavior when no valid approval is obtained
column6: No RFC defines approver substitution, delegation of approval authority, multi-party approval, or behavior when no valid approval is obtained.

column3: Control of approval request volume, grouping and presentation (approval fatigue)
column6: No RFC defines control of approval request volume, grouping or presentation.

column3: Delegation ancestry validation failure semantics
column6: No RFC defines failure semantics for delegation ancestry validation failures. Since ancestry validation is not defined in any RFC, its failure semantics cannot exist.

column3: Unauthorized re-delegation or delegation-depth violations — structural violations of the delegation chain (re-delegation without permission; depth exceeding the limit)
column6: No published OAuth RFC defines failure semantics for unauthorized re-delegation or delegation-depth violations (draft R14(g)).
column7: Gap: requires new normative definition; derived from R11 gaps.
column8: Derived ← R11 re-delegation permission/prohibition and depth limits

column3: Human approval failure semantics (behavior when required human oversight is unavailable)
column6: No RFC defines failure semantics for unavailable or denied human approval. Human oversight is entirely absent from the OAuth protocol model.
column8: Derived ← R13 approval checkpoints and denial semantics (R13.2, R13.3)
